A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same work, renamed from I2VWM to LoT-Pass, and their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. V2 repeatedly refers to an unavailable Supplementary for settings and post-voting results, limiting comparison of that material.

before.justification: V1 reports original watermarking experiments on four open-source and two commercial I2V generators, classical-distortion tests, and an optical-flow ablation in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results and additional frame-drop, latent-space, motion-intensity, and component-ablation experiments in Sections 4.2–4.3.

M1.justification: V2 Section 3.2 adds temporal inversion during training with probability 0.5, using the watermarked image as the alignment reference before decoding. V1 applies alignment only during inference. The encoder, decoder, simulated VAE/warping distortions, losses, and inference voting remain substantially the same; the renamed modules do not themselves constitute new methods.

E1.justification: The COCO, DIV2K, and Flickr2K datasets and four open-source/two commercial generators are retained. V2 adds evaluation after removing initial video frames. Its classical-distortion comparison adds RemoveLines and random bending, while v1's dropout and grayscale test columns are absent.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain SSLWM, CIN, MuST, TrustMark, WAM, VINE-R, and Robust-Wide. V2 sometimes labels VINE-R as VINE, but its baseline description identifies the same method. Newly cited watermarking papers are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported training increases from 150 to 250 epochs, and residual rescaling changes from nearest-neighbor to bilinear interpolation. Classical crop ranges change from 50–70% to 40–80%. V2 also introduces prefix-removal percentages and VBench-based motion stratification. These substantially revise the reported experimental design; they do not independently establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained alignment ablation, v2 tests removal of the temporal-evolution training module, evaluates prefix cropping, and separates low- and high-motion videos. Figure 5 and Table 2 add watermark-pattern and VAE-latent analyses. These investigate several previously untested component, robustness, and mechanism questions.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Reporting averages and numbers of evaluated images or videos does not establish repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Benchmark, image-quality, timing, and classical-distortion results change extensively, alongside new analysis results. For example, Figure 4 changes the proposed method's CogVideoX VACC from 0.975 to 0.966 and Wan RDD from 24 to 49. These are revised results under changed settings, not isolated same-setting gains. Commercial-model RDD values of 120 and 47 are retained.

T1.justification: The shared metric definitions, loss objectives, and majority-voting mathematics remain substantively unchanged, with no new theorem or proof. V2's first-threshold-crossing explanation of RDD matches the formula already present in v1 Equation 24, retaining the 0.9 threshold. Reorganized notation and optical-flow explanations do not establish a new theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds RDD and cross-modal tracing while explicitly acknowledging inability to handle temporal cropping. V2's abstract and introduction center long-term protection against IP laundering through temporal cropping and recovery of distant frames. This materially expands the claimed protection scope, although the bidirectional training/inference strategy already existed.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the signal-amplification explanation with a speckled-pattern/VAE-latent preservation argument and adds interpretations of cropping and motion robustness. V1's explicit limitations concerning temporal order, frame shuffling, rotations, and video-quality evaluation disappear. V2 also introduces the qualification that visually unrelated generated frames should have copyright independent of the source image.

D1.justification: V2 identifies RAFT, specifies the default first-frame reference, discloses a 200-image distortion sample and 480P videos, and clarifies that main results precede voting. V1's explicit training-distortion parameter list and no-ECC statement are no longer provided in the supplied v2. Further details are deferred to the unavailable Supplementary; the code link is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including RAFT, VBench, Sora, Safe-Sora, and Ringet, while removing HiDDeN's discussion and reference. The video-generation discussion expands toward long-horizon drift, but the principal watermarking literature and comparison positioning remain recognizable.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are extensively rewritten around temporal cropping and long-term robustness. Method terminology changes throughout, experimental sections are reorganized, related-work and interpretation passages are rewritten, and the conclusion no longer includes a limitations subsection. These exceed a simple rename.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one, with extensively redrawn motivation and architecture diagrams. V2 adds watermark-pattern visualization and three analysis tables, expands the ablation plot, and revises plot styling and table structure. The commercial-results figure and classical-distortion table are retained with new numbering and placement.

improvement.justification: The added simulation-module ablation and quantitative cropping and motion tests strengthen empirical support and reveal operating boundaries that v1 did not measure. This provides a modest net improvement. The benefit is limited by removal of explicit limitations and implementation details, reliance on an unavailable Supplementary, and a cropped-video superiority claim that Table 4 does not substantiate because it reports only LoT-Pass.
